prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [adversarial] Long headers over tiny numbers (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 4 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Site" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 2: header "Average weekly active users across all platforms" · longest unbreakable word 70px · one-line width 347px
  col 3: header "Median session length in minutes" · longest unbreakable word 58px · one-line width 238px
  col 4: header "Share of sessions that ended in a purchase" · longest unbreakable word 67px · one-line width 307px
  col 5: header "Number of support tickets opened" · longest unbreakable word 58px · one-line width 246px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Rendering convention: the screenshot always shows the WHOLE table. Anything beyond the dashed box is not clipped; it is the part a reader reaches by scrolling sideways, so judge both what fits in the box at first sight and the cost of scrolling to the rest.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

These are all candidate designs you produced, rendered in a real browser:

Design r2B: widths [49, 91, 79, 105, 79] · table 404×262px · row heights [153, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 4/5 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 44px
Design r2C: widths [49, 82, 75, 80, 73] · table 360×309px · row heights [199, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 4/5 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3A: widths [49, 100, 79, 105, 88] · table 422×262px · row heights [153, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 4/5 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 62px
Design r3B: widths [49, 91, 79, 93, 88] · table 401×262px · row heights [153, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 4/5 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 41px
Design r3C: widths [49, 115, 90, 115, 100] · table 470×239px · row heights [129, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 4/5 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 110px

Decide as a designer:
- "preferred": the best design(s). Name more than one only if they are genuinely equally good.
- "acceptable": other designs a careful designer would still publish.
- "bad": designs with clear visual faults, each with the fault. If none of these is clearly bad, also return ONE deliberately bad but plausible alternative as "contrast" widths and say what is wrong with it.
- "ranges": for each column, the px range within which the preferred design stays equally good (keep other columns' proportions).
- "rationale": 2–4 concrete sentences about this table.
- "principles": observations that seem GENERAL (likely to hold for other tables) vs SPECIFIC to this case.
- "tradeoffs" and "uncertain": what reasonable designers could disagree on.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"preferred":["name"],"acceptable":["name"],"bad":[{"design":"name","why":""}],"contrast":{"widths":[int px],"why":""} or null,"ranges":[[min,max]],"rationale":"","principles":{"general":[""],"specific":[""]},"tradeoffs":"","uncertain":""}
